propositions: Push non-fast-forward recovery fails permanently when an untracked local file collides with a file the remote merge wants to create, because the merge aborts and recovery gives up without self-healing.
The merge abort is followed by stash restoration today, which leaves the colliding untracked files in the working tree unchanged, preventing retry success.
Recovery can parse collision paths from git merge abort output and move named untracked files into a shared quarantine directory, then retry the merge exactly once.
The stash commit object recording tracked edits must be restored exactly once on all exit paths (retry success, retry failure, non-recoverable abort) to avoid losing tracked changes.
Genuine content conflicts and paths git does not name should keep existing behavior unchanged (abort, restore stash, warn or raise).
